comment: Authored hero features for Aether Nexus Station's ambient plaza crowd (Phase 9, decision D4). Written by scripts/make-crowd-glb.mjs; the .glb files are reproduced byte for byte by re-running it, and scripts/tests/crowd-assets.test.mjs holds every number below against the file on disk. glTF materials are DISCARDED on load - each part is MERGED into the geometry StationWorld already builds for the 'slot' named in 'bind', so nothing in this manifest can add a draw call, a material or a shader program. The crowd is SIX draw calls for ~180 people and it stays six. 'slot' is only ever 'body' (M.crowd, the garment material, vertexColors: true) or 'skin' (M.skin, flesh, no vertexColors) because those are the only two materials the crowd draws in - a third would be a candidate new shader program on the world where boot time is measured. 'shade' is the vertex-colour value baked on at load for body parts and multiplies the instance's garment colour; skin parts must not carry one, because M.skin has no vertexColors to read it.

standing.note: The three standing body variants (plain, backpack, hood) and the standing head mesh. Photographed at 3.4 m before this landed, a crowd figure was a mannequin: arms ending in the round cap of a capsule, a bare scaled sphere for a head, one unbroken barrel from neck to waist, and a box for a foot. The hands are the part that fixes the first read at plaza distance - the gateway steps put figures at 3-10 m in the entry world's hero framings - and the hair is the part that fixes it at every distance, because a bald ovoid lit by a single overhead key has no self-occlusion anywhere and reads as moulded plastic.

seated.note: The bench variant, whose skull sits 0.38 m lower and 0.02 m forward of a standing one and whose forearms rest on its thighs at a rake of 0.55 rad. Authored as its own file rather than as a translation of the standing one because only the hair moves rigidly with the head; the hands are at a completely different place and a different angle, and a seated figure is the one a player walks right up to.
